current.text: Murray is a projected starter at forward, next to De'Andre Hunter, with Acuff, LaVine and Sabonis. Nobody is pushing that group for a starting spot.
Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan have left the Kings. LaVine and Sabonis are still on the team and still take a large share of the shots.
Experts expect more usage and big minutes for him now that the Kings have cleared out usage. Josh projects about a top 100 season.
He is expected to carry a heavy defensive load.
He is 26 and in the first year of a 5-year, 140 million USD deal. Coach Ham says this is the year he has to prove himself.
Experts say he is going too late at a Yahoo ADP of about 120. Josh is happy to take him in round 10 and calls his ESPN rank of 83 too high.
Experts doubt that his high block rate from last season's small sample will hold. One also doubts that his shooting will come back.
If he reaches about 20 percent usage and shoots better, he can easily beat his draft spot.
The Kings are projected near the bottom of the West, at about 21.5 to 27 wins. They are expected to keep trying to win so they stay out of the relegation zone.
A trade of Sabonis or LaVine is still possible. Either move would change the usage picture around Murray.

durable.text: A finger injury early and an ankle injury late cost him most of last season.
He has made big strides as a defender and rebounder. In a small sample last season he blocked a lot of shots.
His efficient shooting from his rookie season has not come back.
He is a better player in category leagues than in points leagues.
No category is a clear weakness. FG% and assists are his softest areas, and turnovers and blocks are his best for a forward.

note: Murray is a cheap late pick. Yahoo values him at 2 USD and ESPN at 4 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. Experts expect about a top 100 season with more usage on a Kings team that lost Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan. He has no weak category, so he fits any build as a forward who adds threes and blocks with few turnovers. Early in the season, check whether his blocks stay near 1 per game or better, whether his FG% climbs back above 44%, and whether LaVine or Sabonis gets traded.
